summary: Revise at 6.0, up from 5.6. Caiman scores 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. Every gate is now green. The round 1 P0 is closed: verification.json (19:52) is newer than report.json (19:49), template_gate_passed is true at 297,754 B against the 300,000 B budget, there is 1 design.set patch, and its 1,174,126 triangles match report.json. Only two of the six art punches really landed. The crown leaf now has a crisp outline all the way round, terminal tip included, and its midrib runs to that tip. The umbel has grown to five berries. The rest of round 1 is largely unanswered. (1) The ring is still a plain polished D band with one stem pass across it: bare host is well over half the visible outer surface in hero.png, face.png and bare-vs-finished.png, nowhere near Caiman or the Reptilia sheet. (2) The six small leaves are still crumpled, faceted slabs with vertical walls, and they still hang off the band edge as tabs (side.png lower left and bottom, shoulder.png bottom, reverse.png lower left). (3) The rootlets have turned from a sawtooth into radial starbursts of spikes. In hero.png and crown-close.png they read as bristles or a thistle or caterpillar fringe, still thorny rather than gripping. On the palm they read as scattered stitch marks. (4) The collets are still deep straight tubes, and the outer berries' tubes project sideways off the band's side face like a cluster of pipes. The cabochon reflections are still stair-stepped: reference-spinel.stl is unchanged at about 5,800 triangles. Only berries 1 to 3 have stalks, and the peduncle still ends in a hex knuckle (stones.png right). The crown leaf's lateral veins are short cuts that stop halfway, and the terminal lobe shows triangulated shading facets. At 300 px the ring still names itself as ivy, chiefly from the crown leaf and the black berries. To ship, round 3 must close a 1.5-point gap. It can only do so if coverage, the small leaves and the rootlets are all fixed together; anything less is a cut.
strengths: The template gate is fixed and verification.json is fresh and consistent with report.json (triangles 1,174,126 in both).

The crown leaf now has a true, continuous outline, terminal tip included (crown-close.png). The long terminal lobe, the short laterals and the rounded ears still give the stylised ivy glyph at 300 px.
The midrib now runs from the petiole to the terminal tip as one raised rib, and the petiole flows into it from the stem.
Five black spinels in a tighter umbel read better as a bunch of berries in hero-300 and shoulder.png than the three of round 1.
The stem is still a convincing round cable that hugs the band from the crown to the palm, so one plant carries the whole ring.
The body walls have real margin over the 0.8 mm floor (minimum sampled 0.809 mm on the stalks, field thinnest 1.89 mm).

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Ivy only: one stem, ten leaves of one outline family, five black berries, rootlets. The palm leaves sit in a single file along one edge (palm.png), sparse but on theme.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: Marginal. In hero-300 and face-300 the crown leaf and the black berry cluster say ivy. The starburst rootlets along the stem read as bristles or thorns and pull toward thistle or bramble. In face-300 the crown leaf's short terminal lobe is nearly a four-point star.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The crown leaf's outline is now crisp (fixed). But the berries still show stair-stepped reflections in stones.png, all five stones, because reference-spinel.stl was not re-tessellated. The crown leaf's terminal lobe and vein ends show triangulated shading facets (crown-close.png, right half of the blade). The small leaves are crumpled, faceted lumps with no readable outline at hero distance (hero.png left, palm.png).

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as fruit
checklist.reason: Five black spinels are the right fruit colour, but the settings are deep straight-walled tubes. In stones.png the gold walls take as much area as the stones, and the two outer collets stick out sideways from the band's side face like pipes (hero.png right edge, side.png upper right). Berries 4 and 5 have no stalks, and the peduncle ends in a hex knuckle. These read as a gem cluster in tubes, not an umbel of berries.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The six small leaves are still constant-thickness slabs with vertical walls, and they overhang the band edge as square tabs (side.png bottom, shoulder.png bottom, reverse.png lower left). The collets are cylinders. The peduncle junction is mechanical. The crown leaf has a little cupping along the midrib but no lifted lobe tips.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable. Procedural D-shape host, by design.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: It is the only Vepres ring rendered, so it is distinct by default. But in side.png it is still almost a plain circle, broken only by the crown leaf, the berries and small tabs at the bottom.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The hierarchy exists: the crown leaf, then the berries and small leaves, then the rootlets. The density does not. Bare polished host covers well over half the visible outer surface in hero.png and face.png, and the right half of the crown from the leaf tip to the berries is empty. The stem crosses the crown once and has no bark. Caiman and the Reptilia rings are worked edge to edge.

punch_list.zone: Host coverage: crown and both shoulders, theta 0 to 180, especially the bare crown between the crown leaf's tip (about theta 70) and the umbel
punch_list.change: Make the ivy actually strangle the band. Add a second stem pass (the planned z = 2.0 sin(1.5(theta - 250)) climb, or a branch off the main stem at about theta 150) that crosses the crown diagonally under the leaf tip and runs to the umbel's peduncle. Add 4 to 6 overlapping leaves in three sizes (2.5, 3.5 and 5 mm) on short visible petioles from both stems over the shoulders, overlapping the stems and each other. Put fine bark (longitudinal striation, 0.05 to 0.08 mm) on both stems. Keep the template under 300 KB by generating all of this in the existing script nodes.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png and face.png, bare polished host is at most 35% of the visible outer surface, and no run of bare crown longer than 4 mm remains between the leaf and the berries. In side.png the outline is broken by stem or leaf in at least six places. verification.json still shows template_gate_passed true.

punch_list.zone: Small leaves: Leaf 1 to 9 (shoulders, palm, low west, low palm, low east)
punch_list.change: Replace the crumpled slabs. Each leaf conforms to the band curvature and is 0.4 to 0.6 mm thick at the midrib, tapering to 0.2 mm at the margin with rounded edges (no vertical walls). Each carries the crown leaf's outline and a raised midrib plus two lateral veins. A leaf meeting the band edge curls over the fillet onto the side face as a lofted edge leaf, ending at most 0.3 mm proud of the side face. None projects past the edge into space.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png, shoulder.png and reverse.png, no leaf shows a rectangular straight-walled tab beyond the band's edge. In palm.png and hero.png, every small leaf shows the same three-lobed ivy outline as the crown leaf, with a visible midrib, and no faceted crumple.

punch_list.zone: Rootlet tufts along the stem (array #28), theta about 120 to 340, both flanks
punch_list.change: Replace the radial starburst tufts. Each tuft is 3 to 5 filaments that leave the underside of the stem and lie down onto the band surface (at most 15 degrees off the band, splayed 30 to 50 degrees apart, 0.3 to 0.5 mm long, standing at most 0.15 to 0.2 mm off the band), every 1.2 to 1.5 mm. No filament points upward or away from the band.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png and crown-close.png, no rootlet rises above the stem's top line, and the fringe reads as fine roots pressed flat onto the gold. A cold read of hero-300 does not mention thorns, bristles, spines or a thistle.

punch_list.zone: Berry umbel: Berry 1 to 5, collets, stalks, Berry peduncle (crown, right of the leaf)
punch_list.change: Pull the umbel onto the crown so that no collet projects off the band's side face. Cut each collet to a low 0.25 mm rim, so that at least 60% of each cabochon's height stands proud. Give berries 4 and 5 stalks like 1 to 3, all meeting at one peduncle point. Blend the peduncle into the stem with a smooth swelling, with no hex knuckle. Re-tessellate reference-spinel.stl to at least 128 segments round by 64 rows.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png, each berry's black area is at least twice its visible gold rim, the reflections are smooth gradients with no pixel stair-steps, and the stalk junction shows no faceted knuckle. In side.png and hero.png, no collet tube sticks out sideways past the band's side face.

punch_list.zone: Crown leaf (hub theta 110, blade theta about 70 to 115)
punch_list.change: Carry the two lateral veins to the lateral lobe tips as raised ribs 0.12 to 0.15 mm high, matching the midrib, instead of short cuts that stop halfway. Lift the three lobe tips 0.3 mm off the band. Raise the leaf's tessellation (or the stamp's point count) so the terminal lobe shades smoothly.
punch_list.acceptance: In crown-close.png, veins reach all three lobe tips, the lobe tips cast a visible shadow line onto the band, and no triangulated facets or jagged shading appear on the terminal lobe.
